title: India Beat Pakistan by One Wicket in Last-Ball U19 Asia Cup Final
excerpt: Chasing 338 at Al Amerat, India finished on 339 for nine off the final delivery to claim a record ninth title, with Mohit Ulva unbeaten on 49 and Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading the congratulations.
body:
• India chased down 338 to finish on 339 for nine in 50 overs, beating Pakistan by one wicket off the final ball at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman to win a record ninth U19 Asia Cup title.
  • Mohit Ulva, unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, struck the winning boundary off Ahmed Hussain with three runs needed from the last delivery.
  • Pakistan's 337 for nine was built on Usman Khan's 107, Abdul Qadir's 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf's 63, while Kavya Patel took four for 68 for India.
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi called it an outstanding day for Indian cricket and said the team's success would inspire several youngsters.

India won the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup on Saturday, defeating Pakistan by one wicket in a final that went to the last ball at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman. Chasing 338, India reached 339 for nine in their 50 overs, sealing a record-extending ninth title, according to reports carried by Sambad English and PTI.

Pakistan, who elected to bat, posted 337 for nine. Opener Usman Khan top-scored with 107 off 111 balls, Abdul Qadir made 80 off 54 deliveries and captain Farhan Yousaf added 63. The pair of Usman and Qadir added 135 runs for the second wicket before India fought back late, with Kavya Patel taking four wickets for 68 runs and Chigurupati Venkata claiming three.

A chase that kept slipping and recovering

Captain Lakshya Raichandani anchored India's reply with 80 off 101 balls, while Aaryavir Sehwag made 58. Pakistan's Rizwanullah took three wickets for 53 runs as India lost ground in the middle overs, and when the ninth wicket fell the chase rested on the lower order.

Manal Chauhan's 47 and his 57-run partnership with Mohit Ulva revived the innings. After Chauhan was dismissed, Ulva and Venkata took India into the final over needing eight runs. The pair collected singles, survived a stumping appeal, and left three runs required from the last ball, which Ulva sent to the boundary off Ahmed Hussain. Ulva finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, with Venkata on 11 not out.

"Outstanding day for Indian cricket!"

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister, on X

Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the team on X, writing that he was immensely proud of the young cricketers for their performance and for winning the Men's U19 Asia Cup 2026, and that their success would inspire several youngsters, according to Inshorts.

What it means

The result reverses the recent pattern in this fixture at junior level. India had lost to Pakistan by three wickets in the group stage on November 8, and Pakistan had beaten India by 191 runs in last year's final in Dubai. India also went into this final without pace spearhead Ishan Sood, who was ruled out with a back niggle, according to PTI.

For the diaspora reader, the names to note are the ones who decided the match: Raichandani, who held the chase together, and Ulva, whose unbeaten 49 under last-over pressure is the performance most likely to follow him into senior selection discussions.
